item.title: Cabinet ministers advised to avoid foreign travel; Parliament session likely by December 15
item.description: Cabinet ministers have been advised to avoid international travel as Parliament may be convened before mid-December. The government aims to introduce a Constitution amendment bill for women's reservation during the next session. This proposal, linked with delimitation, could expand Lok Sabha's strength significantly. Opposition parties have raised concerns regarding its implications, particularly for state representation.
item.dc:creator: Dipak K Dash and Kumar Rakesh

item.title: After 30 years in jail, former Punjab CM Beant Singh's assassin seeks parity with Rajiv Gandhi's killer in SC
item.description: Balwant Singh Rajoana, who has been incarcerated for over three decades, is seeking mercy to have his death sentence reduced. His appeal references the recent release of AG Perarivalan, a former death row inmate turned lawyer. Senior counsel Mukul Rohatgi stresses Rajoana's transformation during imprisonment, while the Centre, represented by ASG KM Nataraj, counters that Rajoana's historical anti-constitutional statements warrant denial.
item.dc:creator: Amit Anand Choudhary

item.title: Missing businessman's non-bailable warrant cancelled in AJL case, ED to move high court
item.description: A special MP/MLA court in Rouse Avenue cancelled a non-bailable warrant against businessman Dinesh Pandey. The Enforcement Directorate is surprised and plans to appeal this decision in the Delhi high court. Pandey is reportedly involved in transferring Rs 10.4 crore through a shell company to Associated Journals Ltd. The court criticized the investigating officer for using a sealed cover, which is typically standard practice.
item.dc:creator: Pradeep Thakur

item.title: Allahabad high court to hear Rahul Gandhi’s plea against PIL, says Supreme Court
item.description: Supreme Court has quashed an order from the Allahabad high court to investigate Rahul Gandhi's assets. The high court did not consider Gandhi's response before issuing the order, which raised procedural concerns. Senior advocate Kapil Sibal criticized the order, claiming it permitted a witch-hunt without examining the petitioner's standing. The court will allow Gandhi to present his arguments regarding the petition's validity and the petitioner's status.
item.dc:creator: Dhananjay Mahapatra

item.title: Vande Mataram at J&K waqf event sparks row
item.description: Several Muslim clerics who attended a Waqf Board event in Srinagar expressed their regret after Vande Mataram was played. They said their participation did not endorse the song, and they prayed for forgiveness. The song sparked controversy as it allegedly conflicts with Islamic principles of Tawheed, promoting the oneness of Allah. The Mutahida Majlis-e-Ulama criticised the Waqf Board for playing Vande Mataram at a Muslim institution.
item.dc:creator: Naseer Ganai

item.title: Omar government breaks silence on Sheshnag row, says lake safe
item.description: The J&K government asserted that Sheshnag Lake remains completely safe following allegations of construction by the Border Roads Organisation. Forest minister Altaf Kaloo reported that heavy machinery operated away from the lake, ensuring no soil entered the water body. A 12-member inspection team found no tampering with the lake's track as maintenance is performed before the Amarnath Yatra.
item.dc:creator: Naseer Ganai

item.title: PM Modi wants ITI courses aligned with industry needs, jobs closer to home
item.description: PM Narendra Modi emphasized the need for public sector undertakings to establish connections with Industrial Training Institutes. He highlighted the importance of a 'Classroom–Company–Career' approach to enhance employment opportunities for youth. Modi suggested that PSUs should evaluate future manpower needs and strengthen partnership with ITIs to recruit trained candidates. He also encouraged decentralised solar and wind power projects closer to consumption centers.
item.dc:creator: Dipak K Dash

item.title: Cheeni Kum: Poor monsoon hits sugar crop, gross output may not meet domestic need
item.description: India's sugar production for the 2026-27 season is expected to decrease by 15%, primarily due to weather issues. Maharashtra and Karnataka will contribute significantly to the decline following inadequate rainfall. The expected net sugar production will be around 265 lakh tonne, down from nearly 280 lakh tonne last season. Indian Sugar & Bio-Energy Manufacturers Association noted various climatic factors affecting sugar crops across key states.
item.dc:creator: Dipak K Dash

Government’s big manufacturing push: Rs 11,000 crore for infrastructure equipment, six new urea plants
item.description: The Indian government approved a new scheme to promote domestic manufacturing of construction and infrastructure equipment. This scheme will incentivize the production of advanced machinery over eight years, reducing import dependence. Additionally, six new brownfield urea plants have been cleared to boost domestic agricultural production. These plants aim to enhance urea production to meet national demand and cut imports.

item.title: Delhi SIR: Nearly 44 lakh voters may remain off final electoral roll after low Form 6 turnout
item.description: Nearly 44 lakh voters are at risk of remaining excluded from Delhi's final electoral roll. Only about 3.5 lakh Form 6 applications have been submitted by the deadline. Efforts to trace voters categorized as absent, shifted, deceased, or duplicate have seen limited success due to various challenges. The distribution of enumeration forms is ongoing and will conclude at the end of November.

item.title: PRAGATI meeting: PM Modi reviews infrastructure projects worth over Rs 78,000 crore, stresses timely execution
item.description: Prime Minister Narendra Modi led a review meeting on key infrastructure projects worth over Rs 78,000 crore. The discussion included strategies to enhance road, railway, power, and coal sectors while addressing delays and implementation issues. A significant focus was placed on improving the Industrial Training Institute ecosystem through the PM-SETU initiative. Partnerships between industries and ITIs were encouraged to align training with job market demands.
item.dc:creator: Yashasvi Vasistha

item.title: PM Modi asks ministers to stay put & stay ready; next Parliament session likely before December 15: Report
item.description: Prime Minister Narendra Modi has directed ministers to avoid foreign travel and prepare for the upcoming Parliament session. The Cabinet meeting highlighted delays in convening the Winter Session, which has raised questions from opposition parties. The government's focus is on possibly introducing the Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill linked to delimitation and women's reservation in Parliament. Changes in political alliances have altered required support dynamics for passing legislation.
item.dc:creator: Yashasvi Vasistha

item.title: MSME sector: Govt sets 50% registration target for women entrepreneurs
item.description: In a significant move, Union MSME minister Jitan Ram Manjhi shared plans to boost women's registration in Udyam to an ambitious 50%. He highlighted that embracing inclusivity within the MSME sector is crucial for driving economic advancement. Furthermore, the government is dedicated to creating enhanced opportunities for entrepreneurs from marginalized backgrounds, prioritizing access to funding, technology integration, and fortifying global competitiveness across various identified growth sectors.
item.dc:creator: Mahima Sharma

item.title: Aero India 2027 expands exhibition space as demand exceeds capacity
item.description: The Ministry of Defence is set to enhance the exhibition infrastructure for Aero India 2027 due to growing interest in the event. Scheduled for February 2027 at Air Force Station Yelahanka, the exhibition will feature two new hangars and optional mezzanine floors for exhibitors. These developments will allow a wider array of international aerospace firms and domestic producers to display their innovations effectively.
